text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Norway is not prepared for a crisis in the health sector. The state health service says it needs 300 million crowns to improve the situation. On several occasions over the last few years supplies of important medicines have been restricted as during the Gulf War when stocks of insulin where emptied.

- One out of four Norwegians say it is more difficult to control spending when they use credit cards instead of cash, according to a new study. Women in Oslo are persuaded more easily than rest of the population to buy goods, the study shows.

- Knud Soerensen, head of Den Danske Bank, says the Nordic finance market will be dominated by three to five large banks in a few years. Den Danske Bank is interested in acquiring Norwegian institutions, but Soerensen says there will be no hostile takeovers.
- The value of Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA has doubled in nine months. On Monday Kvaerner's A share rose another five percent to a record high of 430 crowns.

- Naturkraft will be granted concessions to build two gas-fired power plants at the beginning of next week, Energy Minister Ranveig Froeiland says. Froeiland says she is not worried that the concessions will be in conflict with the law. Environmentalists claim the government is not allowed to grant concessions to increase emissions of carbon dioxide.
